Orcs communs — Yrch

Les Orcs communs, appelés Yrch en sindarin, représentent la forme la plus répandue des peuples orcs de la Terre du Milieu. Ils ne constituent pas une nation unique, mais un vaste ensemble de tribus, bandes guerrières, clans souterrains et populations soumises aux différentes puissances de l’Ombre. La Culture décrit leur éducation : société tribale et violente, vie souterraine, discipline imposée, pillage, artisanat robuste, embuscade, langues et manière de combattre.

Une multitude de peuples orcs

Le terme « Orcs communs » recouvre une grande diversité. Un Orc des Monts Brumeux peut parler et s’équiper autrement qu’un Orc du Mordor, mais tous partagent assez de traits pour former un socle culturel commun. Cette fragmentation explique leur difficulté à rester durablement unis sans l’intervention d’une autorité extérieure très forte.

Clans, bandes et chefs

La cellule sociale est généralement le clan, la tribu ou la bande. L’autorité appartient à celui qui dispose de suffisamment de force, de prestige, d’alliés ou de peur pour imposer ses décisions. Un chef reste chef tant qu’il peut faire respecter sa position. La mobilité sociale existe, mais elle passe par la guerre, le pillage, une faveur ou l’élimination d’un rival.

Autorité et peur

La peur est un instrument ordinaire de gouvernement. Sous Morgoth, Sauron ou leurs lieutenants, des groupes rivaux peuvent fonctionner ensemble. Lorsque cette pression disparaît, les rivalités reviennent. Un Orc peut servir pendant des années une puissance qu’il déteste simplement parce que la désobéissance serait plus dangereuse.

Famille et apprentissage

Les liens familiaux existent et fournissent protection, alliances et soutien. L’enfance est rude : les jeunes apprennent rapidement à défendre leurs possessions, reconnaître les rapports de force et savoir quand éviter plus puissant qu’eux. L’éducation est pratique, par imitation et participation : chasse, forge, réparation, combat, orientation souterraine, cuisine, pièges et pillage.

Vie souterraine

Une grande partie des Orcs communs vivent dans des cavernes, tunnels, mines abandonnées ou forteresses souterraines. Ils réutilisent volontiers des ouvrages plus anciens sans respecter leur fonction originelle. Leur architecture privilégie la solidité, la rapidité et l’efficacité : étayer une galerie, renforcer une porte et contrôler un passage comptent davantage que l’élégance.

Réutilisation et artisanat

Les Orcs excellent dans la réutilisation. Une arme récupérée est réparée, une pièce d’armure ennemie adaptée, une structure conquise réoccupée. Leur artisanat est souvent grossier mais parfaitement fonctionnel. Les meilleurs forgerons peuvent produire des armes et armures de bonne qualité lorsque les ressources et l’organisation le permettent.

Mines, forge et matériaux

Les grandes communautés exploitent des mines et des forges. Fer et acier deviennent armes, pointes, chaînes, outils et éléments d’armure. Le cuir sert aux vêtements, protections, sangles et fourreaux ; le bois aux manches, arcs, flèches et palissades. Les compétences pratiques sont valorisées parce qu’elles maintiennent la bande en état de combattre.

Spéléologie et obscurité

La Spéléologie est importante dans les communautés montagnardes. Les Orcs connaissent passages, fissures, changements de niveau et itinéraires secondaires. Les capacités sensorielles particulières relèvent de la Race ; culturellement, ils sont simplement habitués à fonctionner dans des lieux sombres, souvent volontairement maintenus en faible lumière pour gêner les intrus.

Nourriture et subsistance

Les Orcs sont opportunistes : viande, champignons, racines, céréales pillées ou cultivées simplement, animaux et provisions capturées. La qualité dépend du groupe. Une garnison organisée peut être correctement approvisionnée ; une bande isolée peut connaître de longues périodes de faim. Bière et alcools forts sont appréciés lorsqu’ils sont disponibles.

Vêtements, marques et statut

Cuir, laine grossière, tissus récupérés et fourrures dominent. Les grandes armées peuvent imposer une certaine uniformité. Dents, os, morceaux de métal, trophées, chaînes et symboles simples indiquent parfois statut ou appartenance. Posséder un objet précieux et réussir à le conserver est déjà une démonstration de puissance.

Armes et armures

Les Orcs communs utilisent épées courtes, cimeterres, dagues, haches, masses, lances, javelots, arcs courts, arbalètes, fouets et armes improvisées. Le cuir renforcé, les protections métalliques, la maille et les casques sont courants selon les ressources. Les groupes indépendants présentent un équipement très hétéroclite ; les armées organisées davantage de standardisation.

Discipline, embuscade et combat nocturne

La discipline varie énormément. Une bande suit son chef ; une armée du Mordor peut employer officiers, unités et signaux. Les Orcs excellent souvent dans les embuscades : passes, cavernes et points où l’ennemi doit ralentir. Ils préfèrent une victoire facile à un duel « honorable ». Le combat nocturne et l’usage du terrain sont naturels à leur Culture.

Pièges, Pistage et Observation

Fosses, alarmes simples, pierres instables et passages préparés protègent les cavernes. Les éclaireurs développent Approche furtive et Dissimulation. Le Pistage sert à poursuivre fugitifs, gibier et prisonniers. L’Observation est indispensable aux gardes comme aux pillards et nourrit aussi la méfiance permanente envers les rivaux internes.

Pillage, commerce et esclavage

Le pillage est une activité économique importante : nourriture, armes, vêtements et prisonniers peuvent être pris lors de raids. Les Orcs peuvent aussi commercer entre tribus, avec des Hommes alliés à l’Ombre ou avec des partenaires pragmatiques. L’esclavage est courant dans de nombreuses sociétés orcs, notamment pour les mines, ateliers, fortifications et travaux de transport.

Tempérament et querelles

Les Orcs communs sont méfiants, agressifs, rancuniers, opportunistes et pragmatiques. Ils peuvent être patients lorsqu’une embuscade ou une vengeance l’exige. L’humour est souvent cruel et moqueur ; insultes et surnoms servent à tester le statut. Les querelles autour du butin, de la nourriture et du prestige sont fréquentes.

Relations

Les tribus orcs sont souvent rivales. Les Uruk-hai inspirent crainte, jalousie et ressentiment ; les Demi-Orcs peuvent servir d’intermédiaires avec les Humains ; les Trolls sont des forces de choc dangereuses à contrôler. Les Elfes et les Khazâd sont des ennemis traditionnels, tandis que l’attitude envers les Humains varie selon leur allégeance politique.

Langues

Il n’existe pas une langue orc uniforme : les tribus développent des dialectes parfois difficiles à comprendre entre eux. Le Parler Noir possède un statut de langue de pouvoir et de commandement sous Sauron. Le westron et d’autres langues régionales peuvent être appris par les éclaireurs, pillards, espions et marchands.

Religion et superstition

La plupart des Orcs communs ne développent pas une religion structurée indépendante. Leur rapport aux puissances surnaturelles est dominé par la peur, l’obéissance et la superstition. Morgoth ou Sauron peuvent être servis comme maîtres terrifiants plutôt que comme divinités aimées. Certaines communautés possèdent des sorciers ou chamans, mais ils restent exceptionnels.

Compétences culturelles

Le profil favorise Armes, Armures, Observation, Pistage, Approche furtive, Dissimulation, Embuscade, Spéléologie, Fabrication de pièges, Survie, Forge, Travail du cuir et Intimidation. Cuisine, Travail du bois, Cordages, Signalisation, Mine, Escalade, Commerce, Estimation et Langues complètent le profil selon l’origine.

La Race Orcs porte morphologie, sens, adaptations physiologiques et rapport racial au Soleil. La Culture Orcs communs — Yrch porte vie souterraine, armes, armures, raid, Spéléologie, Embuscade, artisanat, organisation tribale et langues. Aucun avantage sensoriel ne doit être compté deux fois.

Common Orcs — Yrch

Common Orcs, called Yrch in Sindarin, represent the most widespread form of Orc-kind in Middle-earth. They do not constitute a single nation, but a vast collection of tribes, warbands, underground clans, and populations subjected to the different powers of the Shadow. The Culture describes their upbringing: violent tribal society, underground life, imposed discipline, raiding, robust craftsmanship, ambush, languages, and methods of fighting.

A multitude of Orc peoples

The term “Common Orcs” covers great diversity. An Orc of the Misty Mountains may speak and equip himself differently from an Orc of Mordor, but they share enough traits to form a common cultural foundation. This fragmentation explains their difficulty in remaining united for long without the intervention of an extremely powerful outside authority.

Clans, bands, and chiefs

The basic social unit is generally the clan, tribe, or band. Authority belongs to whoever has enough strength, prestige, allies, or fear to impose decisions. A chief remains chief for as long as he can enforce his position. Social mobility exists, but it comes through war, plunder, favor, or the removal of a rival.

Authority and fear

Fear is an ordinary instrument of government. Under Morgoth, Sauron, or their lieutenants, rival groups can function together. When that pressure disappears, rivalries return. An Orc may serve for years a power he hates simply because disobedience would be more dangerous.

Family and learning

Family ties exist and provide protection, alliances, and support. Childhood is harsh: the young quickly learn to defend their possessions, recognize balances of power, and know when to avoid someone stronger than themselves. Education is practical, through imitation and participation: hunting, smithing, repair, combat, underground navigation, cooking, traps, and plunder.

Underground life

A large proportion of Common Orcs live in caves, tunnels, abandoned mines, or underground fortresses. They readily reuse older works without respecting their original purpose. Their architecture favors solidity, speed, and efficiency: shoring a gallery, strengthening a door, and controlling a passage matter more than elegance.

Reuse and craftsmanship

Orcs excel at reuse. A recovered weapon is repaired, a piece of enemy armor adapted, a conquered structure occupied again. Their craftsmanship is often crude but perfectly functional. The best smiths can produce good-quality weapons and armor when resources and organization permit.

Mines, forge, and materials

Large communities operate mines and forges. Iron and steel become weapons, points, chains, tools, and pieces of armor. Leather is used for clothing, protection, straps, and scabbards; wood for hafts, bows, arrows, and palisades. Practical skills are valued because they keep the band capable of fighting.

Caving and darkness

Caving is important in mountain communities. Orcs know passages, fissures, changes of level, and secondary routes. Special sensory abilities belong to the Race; culturally, they are simply accustomed to functioning in dark places, often deliberately kept in dim light to hinder intruders.

Food and subsistence

Orcs are opportunistic: meat, mushrooms, roots, grain either looted or simply cultivated, animals, and captured provisions. Quality depends on the group. An organized garrison may be properly supplied; an isolated band may endure long periods of hunger. Beer and strong spirits are appreciated when available.

Clothing, markings, and status

Leather, coarse wool, scavenged cloth, and furs predominate. Large armies may impose a degree of uniformity. Teeth, bones, pieces of metal, trophies, chains, and simple symbols sometimes indicate status or affiliation. Merely owning a valuable object and managing to keep it is already a display of power.

Weapons and armor

Common Orcs use short swords, scimitars, daggers, axes, maces, spears, javelins, short bows, crossbows, whips, and improvised weapons. Reinforced leather, metal protection, mail, and helmets are common according to available resources. Independent groups show very mixed equipment; organized armies display greater standardization.

Discipline, ambush, and night fighting

Discipline varies enormously. A band follows its chief; an army of Mordor may employ officers, units, and signals. Orcs often excel at ambushes: passes, caves, and points where the enemy must slow down. They prefer an easy victory to an “honorable” duel. Night fighting and use of terrain come naturally to their Culture.

Traps, Tracking, and Observation

Pits, simple alarms, unstable stones, and prepared passages protect caves. Scouts develop Stalking and Hiding. Tracking is used to pursue fugitives, game, and prisoners. Observation is indispensable to guards and raiders alike and also feeds their constant distrust of internal rivals.

Plunder, trade, and slavery

Plunder is an important economic activity: food, weapons, clothing, and prisoners can be taken in raids. Orcs may also trade between tribes, with Men allied to the Shadow, or with pragmatic partners. Slavery is common in many Orc societies, particularly for mines, workshops, fortifications, and transport labor.

Temperament and quarrels

Common Orcs are suspicious, aggressive, resentful, opportunistic, and pragmatic. They can be patient when an ambush or revenge demands it. Their humor is often cruel and mocking; insults and nicknames are used to test status. Quarrels over loot, food, and prestige are frequent.

Relations

Orc tribes are often rivals. Uruk-hai inspire fear, jealousy, and resentment; Half-orcs may serve as intermediaries with Humans; Trolls are dangerous shock forces to control. Elves and Khazâd are traditional enemies, while attitudes toward Humans vary according to political allegiance.

Languages

There is no single uniform Orcish language: tribes develop dialects that can sometimes be difficult for one another to understand. The Black Speech has the status of a language of power and command under Sauron. Westron and other regional languages may be learned by scouts, raiders, spies, and traders.

Religion and superstition

Most Common Orcs do not develop an independent organized religion. Their relationship with supernatural powers is dominated by fear, obedience, and superstition. Morgoth or Sauron may be served as terrifying masters rather than as beloved gods. Some communities have sorcerers or shamans, but they remain exceptional.

Cultural skills

The profile favors Weapons, Armor, Observation, Tracking, Stalking, Hiding, Ambush, Caving, Trapmaking, Survival, Smithing, Leatherworking, and Intimidation. Cooking, Woodworking, Ropework, Signaling, Mining, Climbing, Trading, Appraisal, and Languages round out the profile according to origin.

Race and Culture

The Orc Race carries morphology, senses, physiological adaptations, and the racial relationship with the Sun. The Common Orcs — Yrch Culture carries underground life, weapons, armor, raiding, Caving, Ambush, craftsmanship, tribal organization, and languages. No sensory advantage should be counted twice.

Availability and character creation

The Culture is available in all four Ages. A character should specify tribal origin, relationship to authority, rivals, and the reason he or she became separated from the band. Orcs live in brutal societies dominated by coercion, but they build, repair, trade, joke, plot, and pursue their own interests. Their collective unity quickly fractures when fear of the master disappears.

Pits, simple alarms, unstable stones, and prepared passages protect caves. Scouts develop Stalking and Hiding. Tracking is used to pursue fugitives, game, and prisoners. Observation is indispensable to guards and raiders alike and also feeds their constant distrust of internal rivals.

Plunder is an important economic activity: food, weapons, clothing, and prisoners can be taken in raids. Orcs may also trade between tribes, with Men allied to the Shadow, or with pragmatic partners. Common Orcs are suspicious, aggressive, resentful, opportunistic, and pragmatic. They can be patient when an ambush or revenge demands it. Their humor is often cruel and mocking; insults and nicknames are used to test status. Quarrels over loot, food, and prestige are frequent.

Orc tribes are often rivals. Uruk-hai inspire fear, jealousy, and resentment; Half-orcs may serve as intermediaries with Humans; Trolls are dangerous shock forces to control. Elves and Khazâd are traditional enemies, while attitudes toward Humans vary according to political allegiance.

There is no single uniform Orcish language: tribes develop dialects that can sometimes be difficult for one another to understand. The Black Speech has the status of a language of power and command under Sauron. Westron and other regional languages may be learned by scouts, raiders, spies, and traders.

Most Common Orcs do not develop an independent organized religion. Their relationship with supernatural powers is dominated by fear, obedience, and superstition. Morgoth or Sauron may be served as terrifying masters rather than as beloved gods. Some communities have sorcerers or shamans, but they remain exceptional.

Cultural skills

Race and Culture

The Orc Race carries morphology, senses, physiological adaptations, and the racial relationship with the Sun. The Common Orcs — Yrch Culture carries underground life, weapons, armor, raiding, Caving, Ambush, craftsmanship, tribal organization, and languages. No sensory advantage should be counted twice.

Availability and character creation

The Culture is available in all four Ages. A character should specify tribal origin, relationship to authority, rivals, and the reason he or she became separated from the band. Orcs live in brutal societies dominated by coercion, but they build, repair, trade, joke, plot, and pursue their own interests. Their collective unity quickly fractures when fear of the master disappears.

Common Orcs — Yrch

Family ties exist and provide protection, alliances, and support. Large communities operate mines and forges. Iron and steel become weapons, points, chains, tools, and pieces of armor. Caving is important in mountain communities. Orcs know passages, fissures, changes of level, and secondary routes. Special sensory abilities belong to the Race; culturally, they are simply accustomed to functioning in dark places, often deliberately kept in dim light to hinder intruders.

Orcs are opportunistic: meat, mushrooms, roots, grain either looted or simply cultivated, animals, and captured provisions. Quality depends on the group. Leather, coarse wool, scavenged cloth, and furs predominate. Large armies may impose a degree of uniformity. Teeth, bones, pieces of metal, trophies, chains, and simple symbols sometimes indicate status or affiliation. Merely owning a valuable object and managing to keep it is already a display of power.

Discipline varies enormously. A band follows its chief; an army of Mordor may employ officers, units, and signals. Night fighting and use of terrain come naturally to their Culture.

Pits, simple alarms, unstable stones, and prepared passages protect caves. Scouts develop Stalking and Hiding. Tracking is used to pursue fugitives, game, and prisoners. Observation is indispensable to guards and raiders alike and also feeds their constant distrust of internal rivals.

Plunder is an important economic activity: food, weapons, clothing, and prisoners can be taken in raids. Orcs may also trade between tribes, with Men allied to the Shadow, or with pragmatic partners. Slavery is common in many Orc societies, particularly for mines, workshops, fortifications, and transport labor.

Temperament and quarrels

Common Orcs are suspicious, aggressive, resentful, opportunistic, and pragmatic. They can be patient when an ambush or revenge demands it. Their humor is often cruel and mocking; insults and nicknames are used to test status. Quarrels over loot, food, and prestige are frequent.

Relations

Orc tribes are often rivals. Uruk-hai inspire fear, jealousy, and resentment; Half-orcs may serve as intermediaries with Humans; Trolls are dangerous shock forces to control. Elves and Khazâd are traditional enemies, while attitudes toward Humans vary according to political allegiance.

Languages

There is no single uniform Orcish language: tribes develop dialects that can sometimes be difficult for one another to understand. The Black Speech has the status of a language of power and command under Sauron. Westron and other regional languages may be learned by scouts, raiders, spies, and traders.

Religion and superstition

Most Common Orcs do not develop an independent organized religion. Their relationship with supernatural powers is dominated by fear, obedience, and superstition. Morgoth or Sauron may be served as terrifying masters rather than as beloved gods. Some communities have sorcerers or shamans, but they remain exceptional.

Cultural skills

The profile favors Weapons, Armor, Observation, Tracking, Stalking, Hiding, Ambush, Caving, Trapmaking, Survival, Smithing, Leatherworking, and Intimidation. Cooking, Woodworking, Ropework, Signaling, Mining, Climbing, Trading, Appraisal, and Languages round out the profile according to origin.

Race and Culture

The Orc Race carries morphology, senses, physiological adaptations, and the racial relationship with the Sun. The Common Orcs — Yrch Culture carries underground life, weapons, armor, raiding, Caving, Ambush, craftsmanship, tribal organization, and languages. No sensory advantage should be counted twice.

Availability and character creation

The Culture is available in all four Ages. A character should specify tribal origin, relationship to authority, rivals, and the reason he or she became separated from the band. Orcs live in brutal societies dominated by coercion, but they build, repair, trade, joke, plot, and pursue their own interests. Their collective unity quickly fractures when fear of the master disappears.

Orcs live in brutal societies dominated by coercion, but they build, repair, trade, joke, plot, and pursue their own interests. Their collective unity quickly fractures when fear of the master disappears.

Les meilleurs forgerons peuvent produire des armes et armures de bonne qualité lorsque les ressources et l’organisation le permettent.

Les grandes communautés exploitent des mines et des forges. Fer et acier deviennent armes, pointes, chaînes, outils et éléments d’armure. Le cuir sert aux vêtements, protections, sangles et fourreaux ; le bois aux manches, arcs, flèches et palissades. Une multitude de peuples orcs

Le terme « Orcs communs » recouvre une grande diversité. Un Orc des Monts Brumeux peut parler et s’équiper autrement qu’un Orc du Mordor, mais tous partagent assez de traits pour former un socle culturel commun. Cette fragmentation explique leur difficulté à rester durablement unis sans l’intervention d’une autorité extérieure très forte.

Clans, bandes et chefs

La cellule sociale est généralement le clan, la tribu ou la bande. L’autorité appartient à celui qui dispose de suffisamment de force, de prestige, d’alliés ou de peur pour imposer ses décisions. Un chef reste chef tant qu’il peut faire respecter sa position. La mobilité sociale existe, mais elle passe par la guerre, le pillage, une faveur ou l’élimination d’un rival.

Autorité et peur

La peur est un instrument ordinaire de gouvernement. Sous Morgoth, Sauron ou leurs lieutenants, des groupes rivaux peuvent fonctionner ensemble. Lorsque cette pression disparaît, les rivalités reviennent. Un Orc peut servir pendant des années une puissance qu’il déteste simplement parce que la désobéissance serait plus dangereuse.

Famille et apprentissage

Les liens familiaux existent et fournissent protection, alliances et soutien. L’enfance est rude : les jeunes apprennent rapidement à défendre leurs possessions, reconnaître les rapports de force et savoir quand éviter plus puissant qu’eux. L’éducation est pratique, par imitation et participation : chasse, forge, réparation, combat, orientation souterraine, cuisine, pièges et pillage.

Une grande partie des Orcs communs vivent dans des cavernes, tunnels, mines abandonnées ou forteresses souterraines. Ils réutilisent volontiers des ouvrages plus anciens sans respecter leur fonction originelle. Leur architecture privilégie la solidité, la rapidité et l’efficacité : étayer une galerie, renforcer une porte et contrôler un passage comptent davantage que l’élégance.

Les Orcs excellent dans la réutilisation. Une arme récupérée est réparée, une pièce d’armure ennemie adaptée, une structure conquise réoccupée. Les meilleurs forgerons peuvent produire des armes et armures de bonne qualité lorsque les ressources et l’organisation le permettent.

Les grandes communautés exploitent des mines et des forges. Fer et acier deviennent armes, pointes, chaînes, outils et éléments d’armure. Common Orcs — Yrch

Common Orcs, called Yrch in Sindarin, represent the most widespread form of Orc-kind in Middle-earth. They do not constitute a single nation, but a vast collection of tribes, warbands, underground clans, and populations subjected to the different powers of the Shadow. The Culture describes their upbringing: violent tribal society, underground life, imposed discipline, raiding, robust craftsmanship, ambush, languages, and methods of fighting.

A multitude of Orc peoples

The term “Common Orcs” covers great diversity. An Orc of the Misty Mountains may speak and equip himself differently from an Orc of Mordor, but they share enough traits to form a common cultural foundation. This fragmentation explains their difficulty in remaining united for long without the intervention of an extremely powerful outside authority.

Clans, bands, and chiefs

The basic social unit is generally the clan, tribe, or band. Authority belongs to whoever has enough strength, prestige, allies, or fear to impose decisions. A chief remains chief for as long as he can enforce his position. Social mobility exists, but it comes through war, plunder, favor, or the removal of a rival.

Authority and fear

Fear is an ordinary instrument of government. Under Morgoth, Sauron, or their lieutenants, rival groups can function together. When that pressure disappears, rivalries return. An Orc may serve for years a power he hates simply because disobedience would be more dangerous.

Family and learning

Family ties exist and provide protection, alliances, and support. Childhood is harsh: the young quickly learn to defend their possessions, recognize balances of power, and know when to avoid someone stronger than themselves. Education is practical, through imitation and participation: hunting, smithing, repair, combat, underground navigation, cooking, traps, and plunder.

Underground life

A large proportion of Common Orcs live in caves, tunnels, abandoned mines, or underground fortresses. They readily reuse older works without respecting their original purpose. Their architecture favors solidity, speed, and efficiency: shoring a gallery, strengthening a door, and controlling a passage matter more than elegance.

Reuse and craftsmanship

Orcs excel at reuse. A recovered weapon is repaired, a piece of enemy armor adapted, a conquered structure occupied again. Their craftsmanship is often crude but perfectly functional. The best smiths can produce good-quality weapons and armor when resources and organization permit.

Mines, forge, and materials

Large communities operate mines and forges. Iron and steel become weapons, points, chains, tools, and pieces of armor. Leather is used for clothing, protection, straps, and scabbards; wood for hafts, bows, arrows, and palisades. Practical skills are valued because they keep the band capable of fighting.

Caving and darkness

Caving is important in mountain communities. Orcs know passages, fissures, changes of level, and secondary routes. Special sensory abilities belong to the Race; culturally, they are simply accustomed to functioning in dark places, often deliberately kept in dim light to hinder intruders.

Food and subsistence

Orcs are opportunistic: meat, mushrooms, roots, grain either looted or simply cultivated, animals, and captured provisions. Quality depends on the group. An organized garrison may be properly supplied; an isolated band may endure long periods of hunger. Beer and strong spirits are appreciated when available.

Clothing, markings, and status

Leather, coarse wool, scavenged cloth, and furs predominate. Large armies may impose a degree of uniformity. Teeth, bones, pieces of metal, trophies, chains, and simple symbols sometimes indicate status or affiliation. Merely owning a valuable object and managing to keep it is already a display of power.

Weapons and armor

Common Orcs use short swords, scimitars, daggers, axes, maces, spears, javelins, short bows, crossbows, whips, and improvised weapons. Reinforced leather, metal protection, mail, and helmets are common according to available resources. Independent groups show very mixed equipment; organized armies display greater standardization.

Discipline, ambush, and night fighting

Discipline varies enormously. A band follows its chief; an army of Mordor may employ officers, units, and signals. Orcs often excel at ambushes: passes, caves, and points where the enemy must slow down. They prefer an easy victory to an “honorable” duel. Night fighting and use of terrain come naturally to their Culture.

Traps, Tracking, and Observation

Pits, simple alarms, unstable stones, and prepared passages protect caves. Scouts develop Stalking and Hiding. Tracking is used to pursue fugitives, game, and prisoners. Observation is indispensable to guards and raiders alike and also feeds their constant distrust of internal rivals.

Plunder, trade, and slavery

Plunder is an important economic activity: food, weapons, clothing, and prisoners can be taken in raids. Orcs may also trade between tribes, with Men allied to the Shadow, or with pragmatic partners. Slavery is common in many Orc societies, particularly for mines, workshops, fortifications, and transport labor.

Temperament and quarrels

Common Orcs are suspicious, aggressive, resentful, opportunistic, and pragmatic. They can be patient when an ambush or revenge demands it. Their humor is often cruel and mocking; insults and nicknames are used to test status. Quarrels over loot, food, and prestige are frequent.

Relations

Orc tribes are often rivals. Uruk-hai inspire fear, jealousy, and resentment; Half-orcs may serve as intermediaries with Humans; Trolls are dangerous shock forces to control. Elves and Khazâd are traditional enemies, while attitudes toward Humans vary according to political allegiance.

Languages

There is no single uniform Orcish language: tribes develop dialects that can sometimes be difficult for one another to understand. The Black Speech has the status of a language of power and command under Sauron. Westron and other regional languages may be learned by scouts, raiders, spies, and traders.

Religion and superstition

Most Common Orcs do not develop an independent organized religion. Their relationship with supernatural powers is dominated by fear, obedience, and superstition. Morgoth or Sauron may be served as terrifying masters rather than as beloved gods. Some communities have sorcerers or shamans, but they remain exceptional.

Cultural skills

The profile favors Weapons, Armor, Observation, Tracking, Stalking, Hiding, Ambush, Caving, Trapmaking, Survival, Smithing, Leatherworking, and Intimidation. Cooking, Woodworking, Ropework, Signaling, Mining, Climbing, Trading, Appraisal, and Languages round out the profile according to origin.

Race and Culture

The Orc Race carries morphology, senses, physiological adaptations, and the racial relationship with the Sun. The Common Orcs — Yrch Culture carries underground life, weapons, armor, raiding, Caving, Ambush, craftsmanship, tribal organization, and languages. No sensory advantage should be counted twice.

Availability and character creation

The Culture is available in all four Ages. A character should specify tribal origin, relationship to authority, rivals, and the reason he or she became separated from the band. Orcs live in brutal societies dominated by coercion, but they build, repair, trade, joke, plot, and pursue their own interests. Their collective unity quickly fractures when fear of the master disappears.
